negative_findings.description: Searched in both Hungarian and English for a tender aggregator or bid-monitoring service specialised in banking, payments, fintech or financial infrastructure procurement in Hungary. negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the run cannot outsource banking/payments filtering to a vendor. Sector filtering must be built in-house via CPV codes and buyer lists applied on top of horizontal aggregators, and recall will depend on our own keyword/CPV quality rather than a vendor's curation.

negative_findings.description: Several aggregators make strong coverage claims that could not be validated without paying: Tender-Értesítő's '1400+ monitored sources' and '78% more notifications than TED in 2024', TenderMonitor's 'EKR + Közbeszerzési Értesítő + TED + 100+ municipal sites', and Tendersinfo's '1.5M+ private tender results'. All are vendor marketing observed via search result summaries, not independently measured.
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage claims recorded as vendor assertions only; no independent recall measurement performed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Procurement of a paid feed should not rest on marketing numbers. If any of these are adopted, a controlled recall test against a known set of HU banking/payments notices is needed before committing budget or treating the feed as authoritative.

negative_findings.description: kozbeszerzes.khf.hu, a distinctly branded and separately marketed Hungarian notice-monitoring service with its own subscription page, returned an HTTP 302 to https://www.tender-ertesito.hu/ when fetched. This is a single observation and is treated as a hypothesis of brand consolidation, not a confirmed merger or a dead site.
negative_findings.result_summary: khf.hu appears to redirect into Tender-Értesítő; independence unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Hungarian aggregator market may be more concentrated than the number of visible brands suggests. Counting khf.hu and Tender-Értesítő as two independent sources would overstate source redundancy and give false confidence in cross-validation.

negative_findings.description: Searched Hungarian-language terms for private-sector request-for-quote marketplaces where banks or financial institutions post non-public RFPs ('ajánlatkérés', 'magán beszerzés', 'beszerzési felhívás'). Only Tender-Értesítő and khf.hu claim private-procurement coverage as an add-on to public monitoring; no standalone Hungarian private RFP marketplace surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated HU private-sector RFP marketplace found; private coverage exists only as a feature of public-notice aggregators.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Commercial bank procurement in Hungary is largely invisible to any aggregator. Private-sector payments deals will need to be inferred from indirect signals (vendor press releases, supplier case studies, regulatory filings) rather than tender feeds.

negative_findings.description: For Mercell, Tenderio, EuroTenders and TenderAlerts.eu, targeted English searching did not surface explicit documentation of Hungarian national or below-threshold coverage. Mercell's material describes national/regional/EU consolidation generically; none confirmed EKR or Közbeszerzési Értesítő ingestion for Hungary.
negative_findings.result_summary: Pan-EU platforms confirmed to exist and to cover the EU broadly, but Hungary-specific depth is undocumented publicly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These platforms may add nothing beyond TED for Hungary, in which case paying for them duplicates a free official source. Depth must be tested before adoption, and TED-only coverage would miss exactly the below-threshold band this cell was created to capture.

negative_findings.description: TendersGo was described in detail in a third-party marketing article on gtbc.net (AI tender-document summarisation, unlimited Hungary email alerts) but its own canonical product domain did not appear in the search results obtained. It is recorded as a pointer, not as a verified aggregator.
negative_findings.result_summary: TendersGo product exists per third-party content; canonical domain not identified in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids inventing a plausible-looking URL. AI-summarisation of Hungarian-language tender documents would be genuinely useful given the language barrier, so the vendor is worth resolving in a later pass.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief lists 'Computerworld HU' as a target outlet. Media-industry reporting indicates Computerworld Hungary published its final issue on 20 December 2023 and was replaced by ComputerTrends (publisher Project029).
negative_findings.result_summary: computerworld.hu should not be treated as a live outlet; track computertrends.hu instead, plus the Computerworld archive for historical backfill.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the pipeline from monitoring a dead domain and losing the CIO-level Hungarian IT trade coverage entirely.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for trade-press coverage specifically of private-bank (non-public-sector) procurement of payment hardware/services — i.e. bank card-acceptance or terminal estate sourcing. No outlet was found that systematically reports such deals; coverage is sporadic and mostly vendor-press-release driven (FinTechZone, ProfitLine, Helló Sajtó).
negative_findings.result_summary: No specialised Hungarian journal covers private-bank payments sourcing as a beat.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed press would expose private-bank sourcing that has no published channel; in practice the press layer is thin and PR-mediated, so signals must be reconstructed from vendor announcements plus municipal/public tenders.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian term 'portfólió' collides with the outlet name Portfolio.hu inside procurement notice titles (e.g. a tender for 'Portfólió és alrendszerek továbbfejlesztése'), polluting queries that combine 'Portfolio' with 'közbeszerzés'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'Portfolio.hu bank informatikai szerződés tender nyert közbeszerzés' returned mostly procurement-notice aggregators rather than Portfolio articles.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must anchor on site: filters or the outlet's own search rather than free-text brand+topic combinations; flag 'portfólió' as a noisy term.

negative_findings.description: Napi.hu was included on the strength of the cell brief and general knowledge of the Hungarian business-press landscape; it did not surface directly in this run's result sets, so its current section structure, RSS availability and relevance density are unconfirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Listed as a candidate with lower confidence; requires a verification fetch.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids presenting an unconfirmed item as an evidenced discovery.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for the sponsor/exhibitor roster of Portfolio Hitelezés 2026 and FinTechShow/BankTechShow 2025. Sponsorship pages exist and name a sponsorship contact and tier labels (Főszponzor, Arany/Ezüst/Bronz fokozat, Kiemelt támogató, Megoldáspartner), but no company-level sponsor list was retrievable from search snippets or a text fetch of the FinTechZone speakers page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Tier taxonomy captured; company names not captured. Likely client-side rendered or on a separate /tamogatok tab not yet fetched. This is a rendering/depth limitation, not evidence the lists do not exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Company-level sponsor tiers are the highest-value signal in this cell; collection must use a headless renderer and must enumerate the per-event sponsor tab, not the overview page.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a standalone Hungarian payments-industry association (analogous to a national payments council or card-issuers' association) using terms such as 'fizetési szolgáltatók szövetsége', 'kártyakibocsátók', alongside Bankszövetség and Fintech Szövetség queries.
negative_findings.result_summary: No independent Hungarian payments-only trade association surfaced. Payments interests appear to be handled inside Magyar Bankszövetség working groups and via MAFISZ/HFA, with commercial conference organisers (IIR, Portfolio, FinTechZone) filling the convening role.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the payments supplier map must be assembled from conference sponsor lists and bank-association working groups rather than from a single membership register.

negative_findings.description: The Magyar Fintech Szövetség (HFA) membership page was identified but its actual member roster did not appear in search results; only the existence of the page and general mission statements were retrievable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Page URL captured (hunfintech.com/membership/); roster content unconfirmed and must be fetched directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The HFA roster is a core deliverable of this cell; it should be prioritised for a direct rendered fetch in the collection pass.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language equivalent was found for a 'savings cooperative association' membership register — the Takarékszövetkezetek sector has been consolidated into MBH Bank, so the historic OTSZ/Takarékbank-era association terms returned no live membership directory.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector consolidation appears to have removed a formerly distinct association layer; no live roster found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect a separate cooperative-bank supplier channel in Hungary; that demand now sits inside MBH Bank's procurement.

negative_findings.description: Searches for chamber and association member directories repeatedly returned commercial B2B data brokers (Apollo.io, Lusha, uzleti.hu) rather than the primary directories.
negative_findings.result_summary: These are lead-generation resellers of contact data, not authoritative membership registers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: They should be excluded from the source set: low credibility, unclear provenance, and personal-data/legal exposure under GDPR.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language aggregator or feed exists that specifically indexes bank/payments IT job postings by named platform (core banking, card management, ISO 20022). Signals must be reconstructed from general job boards with keyword filters.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries on Hungarian platform terms returned mostly foreign (Singapore, US, Vietnam) T24/Temenos roles plus generic Hungarian bank listings; no HU-specific niche board surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for this cell cannot be a single feed; it needs a maintained keyword+employer watchlist across several boards, raising cost and false-negative risk.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian job ads largely use untranslated English platform names ('core banking', 'Temenos', 'T24', 'API', 'PSD2') embedded in Hungarian sentences; there is no stable Hungarian equivalent for most platform terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Observed hybrid usage such as 'Core rendszerszervező' at MKB and 'core banking' inside otherwise Hungarian ad text.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language-only queries will systematically miss postings; every keyword list must pair the Hungarian role/verb terms ('bevezetés', 'migráció', 'szakértő', 'projektmenedzser') with English platform nouns.

negative_findings.description: Site-scoped queries against Hungarian IT trade press (bitport.hu, hwsw.hu, itbusiness.hu) returned no article hits for bank IT contracts or the MBH integration.
negative_findings.result_summary: The query returned only an archived 2021 IT Business PDF and unrelated pages; no live article-level results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These outlets very likely do carry relevant coverage; the gap is a discovery-tooling limitation, not evidence of absence. On-site search or sitemap crawling is required rather than general web search.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language 'supplier call' / subcontracting portal specific to ATM, POS or payment-terminal supply chains was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian subcontracting queries surfaced only generic public-procurement notices and SME grant programmes, not bank/acquirer supplier calls.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Second-tier supplier demand in the payments hardware chain is likely transacted privately (direct RFQ), so subcontracting signals must be inferred from award-notice subcontractor fields and vendor hiring instead.

negative_findings.description: The two richest indirect sources for this cell - LinkedIn and Indeed/Glassdoor - are login-walled and/or ToS-restricted against automation.
negative_findings.result_summary: LinkedIn company/profile URLs were visible in search results only; no anonymous full-content access obtained.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The highest-yield signal (vendor Budapest delivery-team ramp-ups, programme names in employee titles) cannot be automated and needs a budgeted manual analyst routine.

negative_findings.description: Annual-report capex/IT-vendor disclosure was located as PDFs but the specific IT-investment and supplier lines were not read in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: OTP's 2025 integrated annual report and Q4 results PDFs were identified on bet.hu but not parsed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether Hungarian bank reports actually name IT vendors (vs. only aggregate intangible capex) determines how much weight this signal class can carry; must be tested on one report before scaling.

negative_findings.description: No public tender/notice board was found for UniCredit group procurement. Searches in Italian ('fornitori', 'portale acquisti', 'appalti') surfaced only supply-chain-finance products, a login-only group corporate portal, and union reporting — no supplier opportunity listing.
negative_findings.result_summary: UniCredit group sourcing appears to be conducted entirely on closed platforms (reportedly SAP Ariba), with no public award notices for Hungarian subsidiary spend.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Contract intelligence for UniCredit Bank Hungary cannot be collected from a primary procurement feed; it must be inferred from union reporting, vendor case studies, MNB outsourcing disclosures and press.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated KBC Group supplier/procurement portal or sustainable-procurement policy page was located via Dutch/English search; results returned unrelated companies (KBR) and K&H product pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: KBC's supplier-facing procurement channel was not identified in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: K&H Bank is one of the largest Hungarian banks; without locating KBC group procurement, the Belgian leg of this cell has only indirect coverage.

negative_findings.description: Targeted searches for publicly announced CEE regional framework agreements naming Hungary as an included market (banking/payments vendor rollouts) returned no such announcement.
negative_findings.result_summary: No press release or award notice for a CEE-wide framework deal with explicit Hungarian scope was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that regional framework awards are largely undisclosed and must be reconstructed from vendor case studies, group annual reports and subsidiary outsourcing registers rather than notices.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-scoped EBRD or EIB financial-sector procurement notice was individually confirmed in this pass; only the platforms, filters and one EBRD credit-line context (Erste Bank Hungary, Raiffeisen Bank Hungary as partner FIs) were established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Platform-level coverage confirmed; item-level Hungarian notices not yet enumerated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Volume and cadence of Hungary-relevant IFI notices is still unknown, so collection frequency cannot yet be sized.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language searching produced strong results for 'beszerzés', 'beszállító', 'kiszervezés' and 'csoportszintű', but there is no established Hungarian term or public register specifically denoting 'parent-group framework agreement awarded abroad covering the Hungarian subsidiary'.
negative_findings.result_summary: The concept central to this cell has no native Hungarian search handle.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian-language monitoring will systematically under-detect cross-border framework awards; detection must run in German, Italian, Dutch and English against the parent groups.

negative_findings.finding_type: no dedicated public tender page found
negative_findings.description: Searches in Hungarian and English for a GIRO Zrt. procurement/supplier page (giro.hu közbeszerzés, ajánlati felhívás, beszerzés, szállító) returned no dedicated tender or supplier-registration section on giro.hu. GIRO's largest known supplier selection (Nets A/S for the instant payment system, 2019) was reported by trade press, not by a public GIRO notice page we could locate.
negative_findings.result_summary: No giro.hu procurement page identified; GIRO's status as a registered ajánlatkérő remains unconfirmed and must be checked in the EKR ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GIRO is the operator of BKR and AFR — the single most relevant payments buyer in this cell. If it does not publish tenders on its own site, the only routes are EKR/KBA filings (if it is an ajánlatkérő) and trade-press/vendor announcements, which changes the collection design substantially.

negative_findings.finding_type: no procurement page located for a named actor
negative_findings.description: For KELER Zrt. and KELER KSZF Zrt. only generic 'Közérdekű adatok' landing pages were found; no procurement-specific subpage (közbeszerzési terv, hirdetmények) was identified in this pass, in either hu or en searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Buyer-side visibility for the CSD/CCP is limited to the general public-data page; the procurement branch, if any, is unlocated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Post-trade infrastructure procurement (settlement, collateral, connectivity) would otherwise be a strong signal; if KELER discloses nothing procurement-specific, EKR/KBA lookups become the only route.

negative_findings.finding_type: empty listing at time of search
negative_findings.description: Search snippets indicated that Magyar Posta's beszerzesek_palyazatok page currently shows no active procurement announcements and invites visitors to return later.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Posta tender listing appears to be episodic/empty between procedures — an empty fetch must not be read as a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector that treats an empty listing as failure would drop one of the highest-value buyers in this cell; the page must be polled continuously and the archived static PDF notices used for backfill.

negative_findings.finding_type: unconfirmed URL for a high-value buyer
negative_findings.description: The Magyar Államkincstár procurement/közérdekű adatok subpage was not pinned down to an exact URL; only the activity-description and payment-notices pages were confirmed by search results. Recorded as unverified rather than absent.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treasury procurement disclosure branch exists by legal obligation but its precise location on allamkincstar.gov.hu is unresolved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Treasury is arguably the largest state payments buyer in scope; leaving its disclosure page unmapped is a material hole in the cell.

negative_findings.description: Magyar Posta routes tender documentation and bid submission through SAP Ariba Sourcing, requiring supplier registration; the substantive documents are therefore not openly collectable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the fronting public hirdetmény PDF is openly available; detail sits behind authentication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Caps the depth of intelligence obtainable on Posta procurements without a registered supplier identity — a decision the user must make deliberately, not something to automate.

negative_findings.finding_type: no dedicated procurement disclosure found for the deposit insurer/other adjacent state bodies
negative_findings.description: This pass did not surface procurement pages for adjacent state-influenced financial bodies beyond the named eight (e.g. OBA/National Deposit Insurance Fund, Szanálási Alap, Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület, Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal payment functions). No hu-language queries were run for them within this cell's budget.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor map is complete for the assigned eight but not extended to plausible neighbours.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Adjacent state buyers procure comparable payments/cash infrastructure and could be missed entirely by a buyer-name-filtered feed.

negative_findings.description: No national aggregator of Hungarian municipal council agendas/minutes (képviselő-testületi előterjesztések, jegyzőkönyvek) was found. or.njt.hu aggregates only local DECREES (önkormányzati rendeletek), not agendas or minutes, and several municipalities state that minutes are inspectable at the mayor's office during office hours.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in Hungarian for council minutes on bank selection; results were individual municipal sites plus the decree register, no cross-municipality index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The earliest and often the only signal for sub-threshold municipal account/POS deals lives in these documents; without a central index, collection must be per-buyer and will be expensive and incomplete.

negative_findings.description: No specific POS-terminal or card-acquiring procurement notice by a Hungarian hospital or university was located within this run; Semmelweis procurement documents surfaced were for unrelated categories (e.g. SPECT equipment).
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian query combining kórház/egyetem + POS terminál + közbeszerzés returned buyer procurement portals and bank acquiring product pages, not notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cannot yet confirm whether health/education card acceptance is tendered at all or absorbed via EFER/central framework contracts; this shapes whether the cell has a real notice stream.

negative_findings.description: redflags.eu is reported as not updated since 27 October 2023 owing to TED data-provision changes.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search result text explicitly states the halt; treated as historic-only, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents using it for live risk scoring of current municipal banking tenders; a replacement risk-indicator layer must be built in-house from TED/EKR data.

negative_findings.description: EKR document access and bidding require personal + organisational registration; only the eljárástár browse layer appears open. Not verified in this run whether the browse layer is machine-readable or rate-limited.
negative_findings.result_summary: Documentation and guides consistently describe mandatory registration for use; public search described as available since June 2024.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether EKR can be automated or must be supplemented by the gazette and commercial aggregators.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated procurement/disclosure page for Volánbusz Zrt. was confirmed in this run (searches returned BKV and Fővárosi Vízművek instead, plus an archived KMKK page).
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian query on Kbt. 43. § disclosures returned no Volánbusz page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Volánbusz is a nationwide bus operator and a major ticketing-payments buyer; its notices may only be reachable via EKR/CoRe buyer search.

negative_findings.description: K&H Bank (KBC group) — repeated Hungarian-language searches on kh.hu for beszállítói regisztráció, szállítóinknak, beszerzési alapelvek and beszállítói etikai kódex returned only retail/insurance customer portals and the career portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: No vendor registration page, no RFP page, no procurement contact found on kh.hu. Only the K&H Csoport fenntarthatósági irányelvek document describes supplier CSR contractual requirements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: K&H is a top-3 Hungarian bank; its IT/facilities spend is entirely invisible externally. Access must be pursued via KBC group procurement or relationship channels, not open sources.

negative_findings.description: MBH Bank — no szállítói/beszállítói portál, no vendor registration and no RFP page located; searches surfaced only the MBH Beszállítói Faktoring (supply-chain finance) product and the merchant (kereskedői) POS portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only public sourcing evidence is the procurement/bidding chapter of the MBH Etikai Kódex.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MBH is Hungary's second-largest bank and a large post-merger consolidation buyer; the absence of any public channel means its sourcing is trackable only via ethics-code language, MNB outsourcing regime, press and direct contact.

negative_findings.description: GRÁNIT Bank — Hungarian searches on beszerzés, beszállító, pályázat and ajánlatkérés returned no procurement or supplier page at all; the only procurement-adjacent hit was Gránit's participation, alongside MBH and OTP, as a bidder in the MFB Pont Plusz public procurement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero vendor-facing content located for Gránit Bank.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Gránit is the fastest-growing digital bank in the cell and a likely buyer of payments/IT services, but is entirely opaque from open sources; monitoring must rely on press, EKR bidder records and vendor-side announcements.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian term 'beszállítói' is heavily overloaded: at MBH, UniCredit and others 'beszállítói finanszírozás / beszállítói faktoring / beszállítói program' means reverse-factoring supply-chain finance SOLD to clients, not the bank's own purchasing.
negative_findings.result_summary: The majority of bank-site hits for 'beszállítói' were supply-chain-finance products, not procurement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated Hungarian collection on 'beszállítói' will be dominated by false positives; queries must pair it with beszerzés / szállítói regisztráció / pályáztatás / ajánlatkérés and exclude faktoring / finanszírozás.

negative_findings.description: None of the nine private banks in this cell publishes open tender notices (versenyfelhívás / ajánlati felhívás) the way Magyar Telekom does. OTP explicitly routes RFx through invitation-only SAP Ariba events; Erste routes them through the Erste Group Procurements online platform.
negative_findings.result_summary: No open RFP/RFI listings found for any private Hungarian bank.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for these banks, only onboarding/policy pages and platform identification are collectable; award-level intelligence must come from indirect sources (vendor press releases, registry, MNB outsourcing, MFB benchmarks).

negative_findings.description: The MNB outsourcing (kiszervezés) register — the richest structured bank-to-vendor contract dataset in Hungary — is a supervisory filing, not a public register.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 58/2015 MNB rendelet and 7/2020 ajánlás describe mandatory notification and register content, but the data itself sits with the supervisor via the ERA portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on open-source vendor-contract visibility; only the rules, not the records, are collectable. Any future DORA register-of-information disclosure would be a step change and should be watched.

negative_findings.description: erstegroupprocurement.com and epp.unicreditbank.hu/partnerkapu were identified by reference/search but not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs recorded with reduced confidence; scope and liveness unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both are plausible direct vendor entry points; a single failed or skipped fetch is not evidence they are dead or irrelevant and they should be checked in the deterministic verification pass.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, structured registry of vendor-announced private-sector contract wins in Hungary exists; there is no Hungarian equivalent of a commercial 'deal tracker' covering bank/retail technology awards.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in both hu and en returned only scattered vendor newsrooms and trade-press articles; no aggregator scoped to Hungary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be vendor-by-vendor (many small crawls) rather than one high-yield feed, raising ongoing cost and increasing miss risk.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries built on 'sajtóközlemény' + 'szállító' + 'bank' surfaced mostly banking-association and central-bank press pages, not vendor win announcements.
negative_findings.result_summary: Top HU results were bankszovetseg.hu and mnb.hu press rooms plus academic history material — off-cell for vendor announcements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian vendors appear to publish wins under 'referencia'/'esettanulmány'/'ügyfeleink' rather than 'sajtóközlemény'; query vocabulary must be adjusted to those terms.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific card-issuing/processing vendor win announcement was located for 2025-2026 despite targeted search (issuer-processor space).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned generic issuer-processor marketing pages and non-Hungarian partnerships only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card issuing/processing is a core Printec-adjacent segment; absence of evidence here is a discovery gap, not evidence of no deals.

negative_findings.description: Vendor newsroom URLs for NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Intellect Design, GK Software and Barion were inferred from the vendor's known site structure rather than opened during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not fetched in this run; liveness unknown.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These need the deterministic verification pass; do not treat the URL paths as confirmed.

negative_findings.description: No public, structured 'reference list' of banking-sector engagements was found for the Hungarian arms of NTT Data, DXC Technology or Accenture. English and Hungarian searches surfaced no HU-specific banking case studies for NTT Data HU or DXC HU.
negative_findings.result_summary: Global case-study libraries exist but were not confirmed to contain HU banking references in this pass; HU-entity reference pages were not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are significant employers in HU financial-services delivery, so their engagements will have to be inferred indirectly (e-beszámoló financials, bank outsourcing registers, job ads, LinkedIn) rather than read off a reference page.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated public register was found that lists private-sector (bank-to-integrator) contract awards in Hungary. Public procurement data covers only public buyers; private bank IT deals appear only via vendor PR, bank outsourcing annexes, or trade press.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for HU bank IT contract registers returned only public-procurement portals and vendor marketing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Roughly half the cell's target universe (commercial bank spend) has no authoritative source; coverage must be assembled from the outsourcing-register and vendor-PR routes, which are incomplete and lagging.

negative_findings.description: Several key Hungarian terms are noisy: 'referencia' also means credit reference/testimonial; 'keretszerződés' vs 'keretmegállapodás' are legally distinct but used loosely; 'pénzforgalom' spans payments traffic and accounting; '4iG' matches unrelated ticker/market chatter.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query results mixed stock-market commentary with contract news for 4iG; consultancy searches returned thought-leadership rather than engagements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Naive keyword collection will produce a high false-positive rate; queries need to be co-constrained with buyer names, CPV codes or document types.

negative_findings.description: For CEE-regional integrators headquartered outside Hungary (Asseco PL, Comarch PL, Sygnity, Ness), no Hungarian-language corpus of banking references was found; their HU-relevant disclosures appear only in Polish or English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-language searches returned no HU-market case studies for these vendors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-border integrator activity into Hungary may be systematically under-detected by a HU-language-only collection strategy; Polish and English collection is required for these actors.

negative_findings.description: OpenTender data is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial), and Nemzeti Cégtár/OPTEN detail data is a paid commercial product with scraping restrictions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Licence terms observed on the source pages themselves.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cheapest analytical shortcuts carry licence risk for a commercial intelligence product; primary EKR/TED/Közbeszerzési Értesítő collection should be the backbone, with aggregators used for validation only.

negative_findings.description: No public, Hungary-specific list of Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirers or scheme-certified terminal vendors was found. Scheme licensing/certification lists appear to be issued to members, not published per country.
negative_findings.result_summary: EN searches returned only generic scheme PayFac/acquirer model documents and third-party explainers; no HU acquirer roster.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The acquirer/certification universe for HU must be reconstructed indirectly from MNB registers, acquirer ÁSZF documents and trade press rather than from a scheme list.

negative_findings.description: No official public directory of qvik-accepting merchants or of all qvik technical/sub-aggregator providers was located; reporting indicates only a small set of sub-aggregators (OTP Mobil, Raiffeisen mentioned in trade press) but no maintained scheme list surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: HU searches on qvik szolgáltató lista / elfogadóhelyek returned bank product pages and media, not a registry.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: qvik ecosystem participant tracking will need press + provider-site monitoring, with MNB/GIRO pages checked for an eventual official participant list.

negative_findings.description: General web search does not index EKR procedure content or Közbeszerzési Értesítő notice bodies well; payments-specific HU tenders could not be enumerated from search engines alone.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries returned portal landing pages plus one incidental VPOS tender PDF hosted by the contracting authority.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A2 payments tender coverage must run against EKR/KÉ/TED search interfaces and APIs directly; search-engine-based discovery will systematically under-report.

negative_findings.description: Private-sector merchant acquiring RFPs (retail chains, telcos, e-commerce) are not published anywhere public; only the outcome surfaces, usually as a vendor press release.
negative_findings.result_summary: No HU or EN query produced a public private-sector acquiring RFP.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Most acquiring volume changes hands outside public procurement, so award-notice monitoring alone will miss the majority of the market.

negative_findings.description: No public, documented API was found for the official Hungarian registers in this cell — neither e-cegjegyzek.hu, e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu, cegkozlony.hu nor MNB Intézménykereső surfaced API documentation in hu or en searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: All appear to be HTML search interfaces only; bulk access to beszámoló data is offered as a paid dataset sale ('beszámoló állomány értékesítése') and grouped queries require an emailed request form.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume polite HTML scraping or a commercial licence rather than an API, which affects cost, latency and legal posture.

negative_findings.description: OPTEN's public pages describe company-information services and monitoring but no API endpoint/documentation was located; whether a machine-readable feed exists is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched 'Opten Nemzeti Cégtár céginformáció adatbázis API' in hu; results returned service and manual pages, no API spec.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents scoping an automated commercial feed without a direct vendor enquiry.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet register or product page was surfaced in this run; the seed's 'Bisnode' reference could not be resolved to a live HU source.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bisnode did not appear in any of the hu or en result sets executed for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bisnode has been absorbed into Dun & Bradstreet in several markets; the HU entity/product name likely changed and needs a dedicated follow-up search.

negative_findings.description: NAV does not publish a 'contracted partner database' of the kind implied by the seed query; NAV's public databases cover taxpayer status (áfaalany, KOMA, enforcement) rather than contract counterparties.
negative_findings.result_summary: hu search for NAV céginformáció / szerződéses partner adatbázis returned only taxpayer-status query tools and NAV's own üvegzseb disclosure lists.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Contract-level evidence for public bodies must come from üvegzseb/kozadat.hu and the procurement portals (other cells), not from NAV.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian case law and practice hold that the Banking Act (Hpt.) is lex specialis to the Info Act, and courts have accepted that the entire contract concluded with a financial institution can fall under bank secrecy (banktitok), so contract data that would otherwise be publishable under the 5 M Ft rule can be withheld precisely when the counterparty is a bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on 'megtagadható-e a banktitoknak minősülő közérdekű adat kiadása' returned legal commentary describing successful refusals on bank-secrecy grounds.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest systematic blind spot for this cell: banking and payment contracts are exactly the category most likely to be redacted or withheld in the contract-transparency archives, so absence in kozadat.hu or a body's III.4 list must never be read as absence of a deal.

negative_findings.description: As of August 2026 the Magyar Nemzeti Bank is refusing to release its contracts above HUF 5 million concluded since January 2025, arguing it is not a budgetary body; Transparency International Hungary has complained to NAIH and the case is under investigation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple independent Hungarian outlets (Portfolio, 444, Economx, Contextus) report the refusal and the NAIH complaint.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The central bank — a major buyer of payment infrastructure and financial IT — is currently a hole in the contract-transparency record. The NAIH decision, when it lands, will determine whether a large body of MNB contract data becomes collectable, and should be tracked as a scheduled event.

negative_findings.description: No documented public bulk-download or open API was confirmed for EKR, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság databases (KBA/CoRe), or kozadat.hu during this pass — only human-facing search interfaces and, for EKR, an email notification service.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language query 'EKR nyílt adat letöltés' returned portal and training material but no open-data/API documentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for the national layer will likely depend on scraping or on the EU TED/Opentender mirrors, which have different coverage (TED only above EU thresholds) and different lag. Worth a dedicated verification pass and, if needed, a FOI request via KiMitTud for machine-readable exports.

negative_findings.description: K-Monitor has publicly criticised the new state public-spending database as poor ('lesújtó'), per Szabad Európa reporting on the K-Monitor blog.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found via local-language search; the specific critique post on k.blog.hu was not read in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the statutory central register (kozadat.hu / KIK) may be incomplete or badly structured; NGO archives should be treated as complements, not fallbacks, and the critique should be read before setting confidence on registry-derived counts.

negative_findings.description: An automated fetch of https://k-monitor.hu/adatbazisok returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.
negative_findings.result_summary: Single failed fetch; other k-monitor.hu and adatbazis.k-monitor.hu URLs appeared normally in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead page — recorded as a hypothesis, not a verdict. Collection should use a browser-like client for this domain.

negative_findings.description: The aHáló network database was described on K-Monitor's activities page as 'ahalo.hu', but that hostname was not independently confirmed reachable in this pass, and the seeded alternative 'halo.k-monitor.hu' produced no direct hit.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the K-Monitor descriptive page was confirmed as a search hit.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The candidate is recorded with a reduced confidence score; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve the correct hostname before collection is scheduled.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact CPV code set for Hungarian banking/payments procurement was not empirically validated against live notices (only 66110000 banking services was confirmed conceptually).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Once EKR/Értesítő search is reachable, run an empirical CPV frequency analysis over HU notices containing bank/payment keywords to derive the real code set (66100000/66110000 banking, 66172000 payment transaction processing, 79940000 collection agency, 30144200 ticket-issuing machines, 30230000/48000000 IT, 79710000 security/cash-in-transit) and freeze it as the collection filter.

coverage_gaps.description: Special-sector (közszolgáltatói / utilities) contracting entities — energy, water, transport operators — procure banking and card-acceptance services under a distinct Kbt. regime; this pass did not separately map their notice practices beyond one incidental example (BKV).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated sweep of közszolgáltatói ajánlatkérők notices and their own 'beszerzések / nem közbeszerzés' pages, which carry high-volume ticketing and POS acceptance contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian central-government institutions largely bank through the Magyar Államkincstár (State Treasury) rather than tendering commercial accounts; this exemption boundary was not verified in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Determine which entity classes are Treasury-mandated versus free to tender commercial bank accounts (municipalities, state-owned companies, foundations/universities), so the addressable tender universe is not overstated. Sources to check: allamkincstar.gov.hu and Áht./Kbt. provisions.

coverage_gaps.description: Annual közbeszerzési terv (procurement plan) publications — which precede notices by months — were identified only generically via buyer-side pages, not as a systematically collectable set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm whether procurement plans are centrally published in EKR (they are prepared there per the system description) and, if so, add a dedicated plan-harvest job; otherwise crawl buyer sites each Q1.

coverage_gaps.description: EKR and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő publish almost exclusively in Hungarian; only TED provides English versions, and only for above-threshold notices.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design the pipeline as Hungarian-first with machine translation at the analysis layer; do not rely on English keyword filters, which would silently drop most below-threshold banking/payments contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: Purchases made under KEF and DKÜ framework agreements (call-offs) may not generate individual EKR notices, making a material share of state payments/IT spend invisible to notice-only monitoring.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map the call-off disclosure rules for KEF (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu) and DKÜ (IDPR / kozbeszerzes.dkuzrt.hu), and add contract-level collection via CoRe to recover the spend that framework call-offs hide.

coverage_gaps.description: The TED Search API was documented but not actually exercised with a HUN + banking-CPV expert query in this pass, so the real volume, notice-type mix and CPV distribution of Hungarian banking/payments notices is unmeasured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a baseline expert query (place-of-performance=HUN AND classification-cpv IN 66100000..66190000, 66172000, 66600000) over the last 36 months and record counts per year and per notice type.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified mapping was established between Hungarian national notice identifiers (Közbeszerzési Értesítő / EKR numbers) and TED notice IDs, which is required to deduplicate the EU-level duplicates against the national layer covered by other cells.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extract national reference fields from eForms XML and build an ID crosswalk table; validate on a sample of 20 HU banking notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Banking/payments procurement frequently hides under IT and consulting CPVs (72000000 IT services, 48000000 software, 79000000 business services) rather than 66xxxxxx, e.g. core-banking, card personalisation, ATM/POS estate and cash-logistics contracts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the CPV allow-list with IT/logistics codes and add a Hungarian+English keyword layer (bankkártya, POS terminál, ATM, készpénzszállítás, számlavezetés, fizetési rendszer, elszámolás, acquiring, clearing).

coverage_gaps.description: Opentender.eu's Hungarian data freshness is unknown; DIGIWHIST funding ended in 2018 and the dataset may be stale for recent years.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the max contract date in the HU bulk export before relying on it; if stale, use it only for historical supplier-share analysis.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level financing bodies that fund Hungarian financial-sector projects outside cohesion policy — EIB, EIF, EBRD project registers and their tender pages — were not covered in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout EIB/EIF/EBRD Hungary project and procurement registers in a follow-up slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language searching was performed for programme, RRF and financial-instrument terms, but not for TED-specific Hungarian notice vocabulary as it appears inside eForms HU-language notices (e.g. 'ajánlati felhívás', 'tájékoztató az eljárás eredményéről', 'keretmegállapodás').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add these Hungarian notice-type phrases as full-text filters in TED expert queries to catch notices with imprecise CPV coding.

coverage_gaps.description: Prosecution-side and criminal-law sources (Legfőbb Ügyészség / ügyészség.hu, Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal bid-rigging investigations, KEHI successor bodies) were not searched in this pass, though bid-rigging in tenders (versenyt korlátozó megállapodás közbeszerzési eljárásban, Btk. 420. §) is a distinct disclosure channel.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated hu queries on 'Btk. 420 § versenyt korlátozó megállapodás közbeszerzési eljárásban vádemelés' and map ügyészség.hu press releases.

coverage_gaps.description: No sector-specific pass on the actual banking/payments contracting authorities and their disputes — e.g. Magyar Államkincstár, MNB, Közbeszerzési és Ellátási Főigazgatóság (KEF), NISZ, GIRO/Takarékbank/OTP/K&H as bidders — nor on their appearance as parties in KDB cases.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the KDB/KH decision database by ajánlatkérő name for the treasury, MNB, KEF, NISZ and by ajánlattevő name for the main Hungarian banks and acquirers; also probe CPV 66110000/66172000/72000000.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: KDB decisions, ÁSZ audits and GVH decisions are published primarily in Hungarian, with only selective English summaries (asz.hu/en, gvh.hu English pages).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Hungarian as the mandatory working language for this cell; use English only for EU-level layers (OLAF, EPPO, Commission rule-of-law/conditionality reporting) and confirm which ÁSZ/GVH items have English versions.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed machine-readable feed (API, RSS, open-data dump) was identified for KDB decisions, KH decision database, or ÁSZ reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reverse-engineer the KH database's saved-search/query parameters, check for sitemap.xml and robots.txt on kozbeszerzes.hu and dontobizottsag.kozbeszerzes.hu, and test whether the EU-level TED / national EKR datasets carry cross-references to remedy case numbers.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth of the online KDB decision archive (how far back decisions are published, and whether pre-2015 Kbt. era cases remain accessible) was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe the decision database with early date ranges to establish the earliest retrievable decision year and record the archive boundary.

coverage_gaps.description: No aggregator in this cell provides banking/payments-specific curation for Hungary, so sector relevance must be derived by us from CPV codes and buyer identities applied across horizontal feeds.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the banking/payments CPV code set (financial, banking, IT systems, card/ATM/POS equipment, cash handling) and a named-buyer list (MNB, OTP, Magyar Posta, state-owned financial entities, Államkincstár) and apply it as a post-filter across every ingested aggregator feed.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's core rationale is that aggregators surface below-threshold (nemzeti értékhatár alatti) calls invisible in TED. Two sources plausibly deliver this - Tender-Értesítő/khf.hu commercially and Opentender.eu openly - but neither was recall-tested, and the rest are likely TED-derived.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a controlled recall test: take a set of known Hungarian below-threshold financial/IT notices from EKR and check which aggregators surfaced them. Prioritise Opentender.eu bulk data first since it is free and explicitly ingests the national portal.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial bank and payment-processor procurement in Hungary is essentially unserved by tender aggregators; only bolt-on 'magán beszerzés' claims exist and they are unvalidated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not rely on this cell for private-sector deal flow. Route that requirement to indirect-signal cells (vendor press releases, supplier reference lists, banking trade press, regulatory and annual-report disclosures).

coverage_gaps.description: This pass did not specifically probe for aggregators focused on Hungarian utility-sector (közszolgáltató) or state-owned-enterprise buyers, which procure payment and cash-handling systems under a separate utilities regime.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up HU-language pass on terms such as 'közszolgáltatói beszerzés', 'közszolgáltató ajánlatkérő', 'állami tulajdonú vállalat beszerzés figyelő' to test whether specialist aggregators exist for that buyer class.

coverage_gaps.description: No robots.txt, terms-of-service, or API licensing document was reviewed for any candidate. Collection-method suggestions are therefore provisional, and 'collection_allowed' reflects general plausibility rather than a legal review.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before any automated ingestion, review robots.txt and ToS per domain, and prefer licensed API access (Tender-Értesítò) or open bulk data (Opentender.eu) over scraping paywalled aggregator content.

coverage_gaps.description: The khf.hu to tender-ertesito.hu redirect suggests consolidation, but corporate ownership across the Hungarian aggregator brands (Tender Service Group, TenderMonitor, Napitender, KözbeszGuru, InnoTender) was not mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check Hungarian company registry / impresszum pages for each aggregator to establish true independence, so that cross-source agreement is not mistaken for corroboration between what is actually one dataset.

coverage_gaps.description: Only two examples of the local/regional press layer (Civishír for Debrecen, kisvarda.hu municipal site) were reached. Hungary has ~19 county-level media ecosystems (largely consolidated county dailies plus independent local sites) that report municipal account-holder tenders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile an explicit panel of county-daily domains and the top independent local sites per county seat, then run the same 'számlavezető / bankváltás / pályázat' keyword sweep against each.

coverage_gaps.description: No archive or historical backfill route was established for the trade titles (Computerworld pre-2024 issues, older Bitport/HWSW content) which is where multi-year vendor-award patterns live.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test site archives and web.archive.org coverage for computerworld.hu, bitport.hu and hwsw.hu; define a backfill window (e.g. 2015-present).

coverage_gaps.description: Paywalled/print-only trade content (HVG print, Figyelő-type weeklies, ComputerTrends print magazine, BBJ magazine) was not assessed for access route; these often carry the CIO interviews naming systems and integrators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess subscription/licensing options and whether a legal full-text feed exists (e.g. press database aggregators covering Hungarian titles).

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian banking deals was found to be thin — BBJ and Portfolio's English edition are the realistic options; no English outlet covers Hungarian procurement in depth.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Hungarian as the mandatory working language for this cell and budget for translation rather than expecting English parity.

coverage_gaps.description: The bank-side actor map is only partially built (OTP, MBH, K&H, CIB, Erste, Raiffeisen, Gránit, UniCredit, Magyar Bankholding legacy brands, MNB, Magyar Államkincstár) and the vendor/integrator side is barely mapped for Hungary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a formal glossary + actor map file: bank legal names and brand aliases, integrator names, and noisy terms (portfólió, tender, pályázat), before the next collection pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The core member/sponsor rosters (bankszovetseg.hu/tagjaink detail pages, hunfintech.com/membership, ivsz.hu/tagok, amcham.hu directory, ahkungarn.hu member search, Portfolio /tamogatok tabs) were identified but their full contents were not enumerated in this scouting pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a rendered (headless-browser) collection pass over each identified roster URL, extracting company name + tier/category + date, and normalise to tax number for joining against EKR/TED award notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral chambers beyond AmCham and DUIHK (British, French, Italian, Nordic, Swiss, Austrian chambers in Hungary) were not searched, and neither were sector bodies such as the Hungarian e-commerce association, the insurance association (MABISZ) or the securities/market infrastructure bodies around BÉT/KELER.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map with 'kereskedelmi kamara Magyarország' bilateral chambers and adjacent financial-sector associations (MABISZ, BÉT, KELER user groups) and repeat the roster-discovery method.

coverage_gaps.description: Sponsor rosters are only useful as a time series, but historic event pages (pre-2017 Portfolio events, archived IIR Joomla pages, discontinued conferences) were not systematically enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate event ids across years on portfolio.hu and iir-hungary.hu, and back-fill missing years from web.archive.org snapshots to build a multi-year vendor-presence series.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only AmCham and an event aggregator were found in English. Hungarian associations mostly publish rosters in Hungarian only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept Hungarian as the primary collection language for this cell; use English pages only for cross-validation of international vendors and for the bilateral chambers.

coverage_gaps.description: No method has yet been defined for joining association/sponsor company names to procurement award-notice supplier records, which is the whole point of this cell for workstream A2.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a name-normalisation and matching pipeline (strip Zrt./Kft./Nyrt./Bt. suffixes, fuzzy match, then confirm via chamber registry or company register tax number) before the collection pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Career pages were located for MKB/MBH, GIRO and MNB only. Missing first-party career/newsroom feeds for OTP, K&H (KBC), Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit Bank, Magyar Fejlesztési Bank (MFB), and Magyar Posta / Postai pénzügyi szolgáltatások.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-institution watchlist of career URL + newsroom URL + IR URL and enumerate *.karrierportal.hu tenants to catch white-labelled sites.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side newsrooms and Hungarian career pages were only sampled (Dorsum, Mindspire). Not covered: Intellect/iGCB, Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Euronet, Worldline/SIX, ACI, IND/Backbase-type digital vendors, and Hungarian integrators (4iG, T-Systems Hungary, IBM/Accenture/Deloitte Budapest delivery centres).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball the Portfolio Financial IT sponsor/speaker list into a vendor register, then attach each vendor's HU careers page and newsroom as monitored sources.

coverage_gaps.description: No staffing/body-leasing agencies specialising in Hungarian banking IT contractors were identified, although agency-posted contractor ads are the classic tell of a delivery ramp-up under an unannounced contract.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted Hungarian queries for 'IT szakértő biztosítás', 'kölcsönzés', 'bankszektor IT tanácsadás' and identify the top agencies; monitor their job feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: No repeatable method yet for extracting IT/intangible capex lines and named technology partners from Hungarian annual reports at scale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pilot a PDF extraction routine on one OTP integrated annual report keyed on 'immateriális javak', 'informatikai beruházás', 'szoftver', 'szállító'; if vendor names are absent, downgrade this signal class to trend-only.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian vendor hiring (international vendors posting Budapest roles in English on their own ATS - Workday, SmartRecruiters, Greenhouse) was not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each vendor on the register, locate its ATS domain and filter by location=Budapest; these feeds are usually machine-readable and ToS-friendlier than aggregators.

coverage_gaps.description: CIB Bank (Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy) and MBH/other foreign-linked entities were not covered; the cell brief named Erste/UniCredit/Raiffeisen/KBC but Intesa is an equally significant Italian parent for Hungary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an Italian-language pass on Intesa Sanpaolo group procurement ('acquisti', 'fornitori', 'albo fornitori') and map CIB Bank's dependency on group sourcing.

coverage_gaps.description: Group annual reports and Pillar 3 / sustainability reports of Erste Group, RBI, UniCredit and KBC were not yet mined for supplier-spend, outsourcing and intra-group service disclosures.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ingest the latest annual and sustainability reports of each parent group and text-mine procurement/outsourcing/supplier-spend sections with Hungary filters.

coverage_gaps.description: TED / OJEU was not directly queried in this pass, although EIB rules require promoter notices to be published there; utilities-sector notices from bank-adjacent entities may also appear.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a TED (ted.europa.eu) collector filtered on country=HU plus financial/IT CPV codes, and on EIB as contracting authority.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-level 'üzletszabályzat' / kiszervezett tevékenységek lists — legally required to name outsourced activities and their performers — were identified as a mechanism but not harvested per institution.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the outsourcing lists published by Erste Bank Hungary, Raiffeisen Bank Zrt., UniCredit Bank Hungary and K&H, and diff them over time to detect new group and third-party providers.

coverage_gaps.description: Dutch-language coverage for the KBC/K&H leg was only shallow (one query), and German coverage focused on Erste rather than RBI's Austrian supplier channels.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run deeper nl-language ('leveranciers', 'aankoopbeleid', 'inkoop') and de-language ('Lieferantenportal', 'Vergabe', 'Rahmenvertrag') passes against kbc.com and rbinternational.com.

coverage_gaps.description: Magyar Államkincstár's statutory közbeszerzés / közérdekű adatok page URL is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl allamkincstar.gov.hu sitemap for 'közérdekű adatok' and 'közbeszerzés' branches; simultaneously look up 'Magyar Államkincstár' in the EKR ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás to obtain its official buyer record and notice history.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unverified which of GIRO Zrt., KELER Zrt., KELER KSZF Zrt. and MNB fall under the classic vs utility (közszolgáltatói) procurement regime, which determines thresholds and whether notices appear publicly at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extract the EKR ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás for all eight entities and record regime, registration number and notice counts as a structured buyer table.

coverage_gaps.description: IT spend of several cell entities is likely executed via DKÜ framework agreements rather than own-name tenders, so a buyer-name-only feed will systematically under-count.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add DKÜ framework listings and Korm. rendelet 301/2018 scope analysis to the collection plan; map framework holders as the de-facto suppliers to these institutions.

coverage_gaps.description: Contracts under national thresholds ('egyéb beszerzés') do not reach EKR/KBA/TED and appear, if at all, only on the buyer's own site or in its 5 MFt+ contract register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prioritise per-buyer contract registers (e.g. EXIM szerződések, MFB gazdálkodási adatok) as a parallel stream to notice feeds, with row-level diffing.

coverage_gaps.description: Almost all buyer-side procurement content in this cell is Hungarian-only; the English surfaces found (EXIM /exim-en, TED EN) are partial or lag the Hungarian originals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat hu as the mandatory collection language and build a CPV/keyword glossary in Hungarian (készpénzlogisztika, ATM üzemeltetés, számlavezető rendszer, azonnali fizetés, kártyaszemélyesítés) rather than translating English terms.
